r1159104603: Bordered by the Arctic Ocean, Atlantic Ocean and Mediterranean Sea, and separated from Asia roughly by the Ural Mountains and Caucasus.
Shares the Eurasian landmass with Asia and is divided into about fifty sovereign states, with Russia the largest.
Its culture traces shared roots to ancient Greece and Rome, and it drove the Renaissance, the Age of Discovery and global colonisation from the 16th century onward.
r1159104361: Bordered by the Pacific Ocean to the west, the Atlantic to the north and east, and the Drake Passage to the south, with the Caribbean to the northwest.
Dominated by the Andes along its western edge, while the east holds vast lowlands drained by rivers such as the Amazon, Orinoco and Paraná.
Brazil holds almost half the continent's population and generates about half its GDP.
r1159103489: An archipelago of ten volcanic islands off the coast of West Africa, part of the Macaronesia ecoregion along with the Azores, Canaries and Madeira.
Uninhabited until Portuguese explorers settled it in the 15th century, later becoming a key stopover in the transatlantic slave trade.
The capital Praia is on Santiago, the most populous of the islands.
m1159115057: Separates the Americas from Africa and Europe, a divide that shaped the Age of Discovery and centuries of transatlantic trade.
The Norse were the first known people to cross it, but Columbus's 1492 voyage triggered the main wave of European exploration and colonisation.
Connects to the Arctic Ocean in the north, the Pacific in the southwest, and the Indian Ocean in the southeast.
r1159104011: Occupies about two-thirds of the US state of Florida, between the Gulf of Mexico and the Atlantic Ocean, giving it the longest coastline in the contiguous US.
Spanish explorer Juan Ponce de León made landfall here in 1513, and St. Augustine, founded in 1565, is the oldest continuously inhabited European settlement in the US.
Major cities on the peninsula include Miami, Tampa and Orlando.
r1159104273: An archipelagic nation of 32 atolls and islands straddling the equator and the 180th meridian in the central Pacific.
Its easternmost islands sit in UTC+14, the most advanced time zone on Earth, because the International Date Line swings far east around the country.
Annexed as a British protectorate in 1892 and independent since 1979; most of the population lives on Tarawa.
r1730073191: An archipelagic nation of coral atolls in Micronesia, with 98.47% of its territory being lagoon waters, the highest ratio of water to land of any sovereign state.
Settled by Austronesian peoples as early as the 2nd millennium BC.
Named after British captain John Marshall, who explored the region in 1788; it was a German, then Japanese, then American-administered territory before independence.
r1159104297: Stretch roughly 1,200 km across France, Switzerland, Italy, Austria and other Alpine countries, from Nice to Vienna.
Formed over tens of millions of years as the African and Eurasian plates collided, pushing marine sedimentary rock into peaks like Mont Blanc and the Matterhorn.
Hannibal famously crossed the range with elephants, and it later became the birthplace of modern mountaineering and winter tourism.
m1159115831: An arm of the Atlantic enclosed by Scandinavia and the North/Central European Plain, and the world's largest brackish water basin.
Drains through the Danish Straits into the Kattegat, with limited exchange with the open Atlantic.
Connected artificially to the White Sea and, via the Kiel Canal, to the North Sea.
r1159104347: A narrow land bridge between Mexico and Colombia, bordered by the Caribbean to the east and the Pacific to the southwest.
High volcanic and seismic activity here stems from the Central America Volcanic Arc and several active fault lines.
Spanish colonisation began in 1502; most of the region later formed the short-lived Federal Republic of Central America before splitting into separate states.
r1159103999: A peninsula on the Black Sea's northern coast, linked to mainland Ukraine by the Isthmus of Perekop and to Russia by the Crimean Bridge since 2018.
Historically on the boundary between the Greek/Roman/Byzantine world and the Eurasian steppe, later home to the Crimean Khanate.
Annexed by Russia in 2014, a move internationally unrecognised, with Ukraine still considered its de jure sovereign.
vQ584: Rises in the Swiss Alps and flows through Lake Constance, forming stretches of the Swiss, Liechtenstein, Austrian and French borders before reaching the Netherlands and the North Sea.
Carries Europe's most powerful waterfall, the Rhine Falls, and has been a vital trade route since Roman times.
Major cities on its banks include Basel, Strasbourg, Cologne and Rotterdam.
e1159105301: A dormant stratovolcano in Tanzania and the highest mountain in Africa, as well as the tallest free-standing mountain in the world.
First climbed to its highest point, Uhuru Peak, in 1889 by German geographer Hans Meyer.
Formed by volcanic activity linked to the East African Rift, it carries Africa's largest glaciers, which have lost over 80% of their ice in the past century.
r1159104351: Spans North Asia from the Ural Mountains to the Pacific, covering about three-quarters of Russia's territory though home to only a quarter of its population.
Conquered by Russia between 1582 and 1778, starting with the fall of the Khanate of Sibir.
Known for extremely harsh winters, with January averages around -25°C.
vQ1497: Flows about 3,766 km from Lake Itasca in Minnesota south to the Gulf of Mexico, draining most of the US between the Rockies and Appalachians.
Served as a major transport and trade artery and a frontier for westward US expansion in the 19th century.
Its final capture by Union forces during the Civil War was a turning point toward Union victory.
r1159104329: A peninsula and cultural region of northern Europe usually comprising Norway, Sweden and Denmark, with strong shared history and language.
Geography ranges from Norwegian fjords and mountains to Denmark's flat lowlands.
Base of the Viking Age, when Scandinavian seafarers raided, traded and explored as far as North America.
p1159104869: A southern Caribbean island roughly 65 km north of Venezuela, forming part of the ABC islands with Aruba and Bonaire.
Colonised by the Dutch in 1634, who turned it into a hub of the Atlantic slave trade and later a major oil refining centre after 1914.
Known for its liqueur Curaçao, flavoured with the peel of the local laraha citrus fruit.
r1159103801: The second-largest and northernmost of Japan's four main islands, separated from Honshu by the Tsugaru Strait and linked to it by the Seikan Tunnel.
Originally inhabited by the indigenous Ainu people before Japanese annexation and colonisation in 1869.
Its capital, Sapporo, is the island's largest city.
l1159126747: A landlocked salt lake on the Jordan-Israel-West Bank border, fed mainly by the Jordan River, with shores at the lowest land elevation on Earth.
About 9.6 times saltier than the ocean, making swimming feel like floating and leaving the water largely lifeless.
Rapidly shrinking: its surface area has fallen from 1,050 km2 in 1930 to about 605 km2 today.
vQ7348: Rises in Tibet and flows through Kashmir and Pakistan to empty into the Arabian Sea near Karachi.
Cradle of the Bronze Age Indus Valley Civilisation in the 3rd millennium BC, one of the world's earliest urban cultures.
Its headwaters mark the collision zone between the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates that raised the Himalayas.
r1159103769: A Maritime province on Canada's east coast, comprising a peninsula and Cape Breton Island linked to the mainland by the Isthmus of Chignecto.
Settled by the Mi'kmaq before becoming the French colony of Acadia in 1605; Britain later deported the French-speaking Acadians en masse.
Its capital, Halifax, holds over 45% of the province's population.
m1159117123: An arm of the Mediterranean between Greece and Turkey, connected north to the Sea of Marmara and Black Sea via the Dardanelles and Bosphorus.
Cradle of Ancient Greek civilisation, whose many islands - including Crete, Rhodes and the Cyclades - linked Europe and Asia.
Later passed through Roman, Byzantine and Ottoman control before modern Greece and Turkey emerged on its shores.
r1159104359: A subregion of Oceania made up of over 1,000 islands scattered across the central and southern Pacific, including Hawaii at its northern vertex.
Its name, coined in 1756, groups islands sharing related Polynesian languages, culture and traditions.
r1159104125: The third-largest island in the world, split between Indonesia (as Kalimantan), Malaysia and Brunei, and crossed by the equator.
Home to some of the world's oldest tropical rainforests and high levels of biodiversity and endemic species.
Historically ruled by coastal sultanates such as Brunei and Sulu, while the interior remained governed by diverse indigenous communities.
e1159105623: An active stratovolcano on Honshu and the highest mountain in Japan, visible from Tokyo on clear days.
Last erupted in 1707-1708 and is revered as one of Japan's Three Holy Mountains.
A UNESCO World Heritage cultural site since 2013, long inspiring Japanese art, poetry and pilgrimage.
r1159103353: A historic cultural region split between northwestern Russia and eastern Finland.
Long contested between Russia, Finland and Sweden, shaping the identity of both modern countries.
r1159104651: A Portuguese archipelago of nine volcanic islands in the Atlantic, about 1,400 km west of mainland Portugal.
Sits at the Azores triple junction, where the North American, Eurasian and Nubian tectonic plates meet.
Mount Pico, on Pico island, is Portugal's highest point at 2,351 m.
m1159115399: A marginal sea of the Atlantic bounded by the US Gulf Coast, Mexico and Cuba, connected to the Atlantic via the Straits of Florida and to the Caribbean via the Yucatán Channel.
One of the world's largest offshore petroleum production regions, supplying 14% of US crude oil output.
Its moisture drives severe weather across the US, including storms in Tornado Alley.
r1159103941: Stretches nearly 500 km along the France-Spain border from the Cantabrian Mountains to the Mediterranean, with the microstate of Andorra sandwiched between the two countries.
Its highest point, Aneto, reaches 3,404 m.
Historically straddled by the Crown of Aragon and the Kingdom of Navarre, which extended on both sides of the range.
r1159103797: The smallest of Japan's four main islands, lying south of Honshu and northeast of Kyushu.
Its name, meaning 'four provinces', refers to the four historic provinces that made up the island.
vQ35591: Flows from the Armenian Highlands through the Syrian and Arabian deserts, joining the Euphrates before reaching the Persian Gulf, together defining Mesopotamia.
Passes historic cities including Mosul, Samarra and Baghdad and nurtured the ancient Assyrian Empire.
Faces modern threats from dam building, water mismanagement and climate change.
e1159105949: The highest mountain in the Alps and in Europe outside the Caucasus, straddling the France-Italy border.
Ownership of its summit has long been disputed between France and Italy.
The 11.6 km Mont Blanc Tunnel beneath it, built between 1957 and 1965, is a major transalpine transport route.
vQ40855: Rises near Smolensk, Russia, and flows through Belarus and Ukraine to the Black Sea, making it the longest river in both countries.
Noted for major Soviet-era hydroelectric dams and reservoirs; the Chernobyl disaster occurred on its tributary, the Pripyat.
Parts of the river formed defensive front lines during the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine.
vQ40059: Flows from the Sea of Galilee south to the Dead Sea through the Levant, bordered by Jordan, Israel, the West Bank and Syria.
Holds major religious significance: the Israelites are said to have crossed it into the Promised Land, and Jesus was baptised in its waters.
Both Jordan and the West Bank take their names from the river.
vQ1644: Rises in the Czech Giant Mountains, crosses Bohemia and Germany, and empties into the North Sea near Hamburg.
Its catchment, spanning mainly Germany and the Czech Republic, is home to 24.4 million people and cities including Berlin, Prague and Dresden.
vQ548: Poland's longest river, rising at Barania Góra and flowing north through Kraków and Warsaw to the Baltic Sea near Gdańsk.
So central to national identity that 'Land on the Vistula' is used as a synonym for Poland.
Gave its name to the Weichselian (Vistulian) glaciation, the last glacial period in northern Europe.
r1159102803: The largest of Greece's Dodecanese islands, northeast of Crete, once home to the Colossus of Rhodes, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
Ruled by the Knights of Saint John from 1310 to 1522, giving it the nickname 'Island of the Knights'.
Its medieval Old Town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
r1159102839: A Norwegian volcanic island in the Arctic Ocean with no permanent population, partly covered by glaciers around the Beerenberg volcano.
Home to Beerenberg, the world's northernmost active subaerial volcano.
Formed by the Jan Mayen hotspot and classified by geologists as a microcontinent.
e1159105953: The highest mountain in Russia and in Europe, a dormant twin-summited stratovolcano in the Caucasus.
Its eastern summit was first climbed in 1829 and the higher western summit in 1874 by a British-led expedition.
m1159116377: Part of the Mediterranean off Italy's western coast, named after the ancient Tyrrhenian people, identified with the Etruscans.
e1159105729: The second-highest mountain on Earth after Everest, straddling the Pakistan-China border in the Karakoram range.
Nicknamed the 'Savage Mountain' for its brutal difficulty; historically about one climber died for every four who reached the summit.
First summited in 1954 by Italian climbers Lino Lacedelli and Achille Compagnoni.
vQ46841: Flows about 4,294 km through the Russian Far East to the Arctic Ocean, the longest river entirely within Russia.
Its basin lies almost entirely over permafrost.
p1159104887: A waterfall on the Zambezi River on the Zambia-Zimbabwe border, 1,708 m wide and one of the world's largest.
Known locally as 'Mosi-oa-Tunya' ('the smoke that thunders'); named Victoria Falls by Scottish missionary David Livingstone in 1855.
vQ1229: The fifth-longest river in Europe, flowing from central Russia to the Sea of Azov.
Important historically for Byzantine-era trade, with the Volga-Don Canal later linking it to the Volga.
m1159119155: A narrow strait in northwestern Turkey linking the Sea of Marmara to the Aegean, forming part of the Asia-Europe boundary alongside the Bosphorus.
Site of the deadly Gallipoli campaign in World War I.
The first fixed crossing, the 1915 Çanakkale Bridge, opened in 2022.
vQ643: Italy's longest river, flowing from the Cottian Alps eastward across northern Italy to a delta on the Adriatic near Venice.
Passes through Turin, Piacenza and Ferrara and is linked to Milan by canals partly designed by Leonardo da Vinci.
Divided the Roman territory of Cisalpine Gaul into Cispadane and Transpadane regions.
l1159113005: One of the five Great Lakes, the only one located entirely within the United States.
Hydrologically joined to Lake Huron via the Straits of Mackinac, together forming the world's largest freshwater lake by area.
Major port cities on its shores include Chicago and Milwaukee.
m1159115749: A gulf of the northeast Atlantic along the coasts of France and Spain, known for rough seas and reaching depths over 4,700 m.
m1159116835: A narrow strait between the Malay Peninsula and Sumatra linking the Indian and Pacific Oceans.
The busiest shipping strait in the world, carrying about a quarter of global traded goods including oil and coal.
Historically fought over by powers such as the Srivijaya empire, the Malacca Sultanate and the British Straits Settlements.
p1159105165: A rocky headland on South Africa's Cape Peninsula, often mistaken for Africa's southernmost point, which is actually Cape Agulhas further east.
First rounded by Portuguese explorer Bartolomeu Dias in 1487, opening a sea route to the Far East.
Marks where ships begin travelling more eastward than southward along Africa's coast, making it a key waypoint on old trade routes.
m1159116231: A marginal sea of the Arctic Ocean north of Siberia, between the Barents Sea and the Laptev Sea.
Ice-bound for all but about two months a year, yet holds significant undeveloped oil and gas reserves.
r1159102821: A Spanish island in the Mediterranean off the Iberian coast, one of the Balearic Islands and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Famous worldwide for its nightlife and electronic dance music club scene.
vQ78707: The fifth-longest river system in the world and the largest draining into the Arctic Ocean, flowing from Mongolia through Siberia.
Its basin includes Lake Baikal, the world's deepest lake.
r1159103393: An island in the Lesser Sunda chain, divided between Indonesia's West Timor and the independent nation of Timor-Leste.
Formerly split between Dutch and Portuguese colonial rule; Timor-Leste was occupied by Indonesia from 1975 to 1999.
p1159105073: An uninhabited, glacier-covered volcanic island in the South Atlantic and the world's most remote island, a Norwegian dependency since 1930.
First sighted in 1739 by French navigator Jean-Baptiste Bouvet de Lozier but not landed on reliably for nearly two centuries.
r1159104641: A peninsula forming continental Denmark and part of northern Germany, stretching from the Grenen spit to the Elbe.
Crossed by the Kiel Canal, the world's busiest artificial waterway, so ships can avoid sailing around the peninsula to reach the Baltic.
West Jutland is flat and heath-covered, while the east is more fertile with lakes and forests.
r1159104185: A mountain range spanning Pakistan, China and India, containing four of the world's fourteen 'eight-thousanders' including K2.
The most heavily glaciated area on Earth outside the polar regions, with the Siachen and Biafo glaciers among the longest outside them.
Bounded by the Yarkand and Karakash rivers to the north and the Pamir Mountains and Hindu Kush to the west.
e1159106297: The highest mountain peak in North America, in Alaska's Alaska Range, with one of the greatest vertical rises above surrounding terrain on Earth.
Long known as Denali by the Koyukon people before being renamed Mount McKinley in 1896; the US federal name has since switched between Denali and McKinley.
First verifiably summited in 1913 by Hudson Stuck, Harry Karstens, Walter Harper and Robert Tatum.
r1159103669: A peninsula in East Asia bordered by China and Russia and separated from Japan by the Korea Strait, divided since 1945 into North and South Korea.
Home to a continuous line of Korean kingdoms since antiquity, including Goguryeo, Silla and the Joseon dynasty founded in 1392.
The division at the 38th parallel led to the Korean War of 1950-1953.
p1159105053: A waterfall system on the Iguazu River on the Argentina-Brazil border, forming the largest waterfall system in the world.
Most of the falls lie on the Argentine side, though the river flows mostly through Brazil before reaching them.
Protected as a UNESCO World Heritage Site on both the Argentine and Brazilian sides since the mid-1980s.
r1159103857: A Russian Arctic archipelago between the Barents and Kara Seas, with its northern cape marking the easternmost point of Europe.
Used by the Soviet Union as one of its two main nuclear test sites, including the 1961 detonation of the Tsar Bomba, the most powerful nuclear weapon ever tested.
r1159103261: A desert and semi-desert region in southern Israel, with Beersheba as its largest city and Eilat on the Gulf of Aqaba at its southern tip.
Home to the Ben-Gurion University of the Negev and its desert research institutes.
Features sites like the Makhtesh Ramon crater and the ancient desert cities of the Incense Road.
l1159114609: The largest lake in Central Europe, located in Hungary's Transdanubian region.
Its northern shore is a historic wine region, while the flatter southern shore developed into a popular resort area.
r1159102795: Denmark's largest and most populous island, home to the capital Copenhagen.
Linked by bridges to Funen, Amager and, via the Øresund Bridge, to Scania in Sweden.
Comprises about 40% of Denmark's total population.
m1159115483: An Arctic marginal sea between Baffin Island and Greenland, connected to the Atlantic via the Davis Strait.
Ice-covered most of the year, except for a summer polynya called the North Water that supports most of its marine life.
r1159103779: The largest island in Canada and the fifth-largest in the world, located in Nunavut.
Inhabited for at least 3,000 years; its capital-area settlement, Iqaluit, sits on Frobisher Bay at the island's southern tip.
m1159115359: An Arctic marginal sea north of Alaska and Canada's Northwest Territories, named after hydrographer Sir Francis Beaufort.
Receives the Mackenzie River and holds significant undersea oil and gas reserves discovered between the 1950s and 1980s.
Frozen most of the year, though the ice-free season has grown substantially due to Arctic climate change.
vQ8197: Rises in Russia's Valdai Hills near the Volga's source and flows through Belarus and Latvia into the Gulf of Riga.
Latvia's capital, Riga, straddles its estuary and serves as a major port on the river.
m1159118853: A strait between Yemen and the Horn of Africa linking the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and Indian Ocean.
A major global chokepoint for shipping between Europe and Asia via the Suez Canal.
r1159102849: A remote Yemeni island in the Indian Ocean, geologically part of Africa though administered by Yemen.
Famous for extreme endemism, with about a third of its plant species found nowhere else, earning it the nickname 'the most alien-looking place on Earth'.
A UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2008.
e1159107245: A volcanic caldera in the Sunda Strait between Java and Sumatra, formed after the catastrophic 1883 eruption destroyed most of the original island.
A new island, Anak Krakatoa ('Child of Krakatoa'), emerged from the caldera in 1927 and later caused the deadly 2018 Sunda Strait tsunami after a partial collapse.
r1159104077: The 12th-largest desert in the world, covering about 70% of Turkmenistan.
Its name means 'black sand', referring to shale-rich sand beneath the surface, and it is extremely sparsely populated and dry.
vQ2251: The largest river in the Pacific Northwest, rising in British Columbia and flowing through Washington and Oregon to the Pacific.
Central to Indigenous life and salmon runs for thousands of years before becoming a major hydropower and navigation route.
First charted by American captain Robert Gray in 1792, whose ship gave the river its name.
e1159105705: The seventh-highest mountain in the world and the highest point located entirely within one country, Nepal.
First climbed in 1960 by a Swiss-Austrian-Nepali expedition.
Separated from neighboring Annapurna by the Kali Gandaki Gorge, the world's deepest gorge.
m1159116479: A marginal sea of the Pacific separating Mexico's Baja California peninsula from the mainland, also called the Sea of Cortés.
One of the most ecologically diverse seas on Earth, home to over 5,000 species of micro-invertebrates, with parts listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
e1159105297: The second-highest mountain in Africa and the namesake of Kenya, just south of the equator.
A volcano whose ice cap has eroded heavily since formation, leaving radiating valleys and rapidly shrinking glaciers that may vanish by 2050.
Designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1997 for its ecological significance.
vQ127892: South America's second-longest river after the Amazon, flowing through Brazil, Paraguay and Argentina.
Joins the Paraguay and Uruguay rivers to form the Río de la Plata before reaching the Atlantic.
First navigated by Europeans in 1526 by Venetian explorer Sebastian Cabot.
r1159103991: A roughly 6,500 km chain of connected depressions running from Syria through the Red Sea to Mozambique.
Named by British geologist John Walter Gregory in 1896, building on earlier work identifying the linked rift system.
Includes the East African Rift, home to many of Africa's great lakes and volcanoes.
l1159113145: A lake shared by Uganda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Africa's sixth-largest lake.
The second-largest of Uganda's Great Lakes, once renamed Lake Mobutu Sese Seko under Congo's former dictator.
vQ183078: Australia's longest river, rising in the Australian Alps and forming much of the New South Wales-Victoria border before reaching South Australia.
Together with the Murrumbidgee, Darling and other tributaries, forms the Murray-Darling Basin, Australia's most important irrigated farming region.
Empties into the Southern Ocean through the Murray Mouth near Goolwa.
vQ191314: India's second-longest river after the Ganges, flowing east from Maharashtra to the Bay of Bengal.
Nicknamed the Dakshina Ganga ('Southern Ganges') for its size and importance to peninsular India.
Its delta is one of the most densely populated and flood-prone river deltas in India.
r1159102901: A crescent-shaped chain of mostly dormant volcanic peaks in the northwest Pacific, divided between the US territory of Guam and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands.
Home to the indigenous Chamorro people, who likely arrived via one of the longest ocean voyages in early human history.
First reached by Europeans during Ferdinand Magellan's expedition in the early 16th century.
vQ26076: Myanmar's principal river and most important commercial waterway, flowing the length of the country to the Andaman Sea.
Home to the endangered Irrawaddy dolphin, whose habitat is threatened by planned hydroelectric dams including the Myitsone Dam.
r1159103771: The largest and most populous Pacific island along the Americas' west coast, part of British Columbia, Canada.
Home to Victoria, the provincial capital, and one of Canada's mildest climates, warm enough in places to grow olives.
Named after British naval captain George Vancouver, who explored the Pacific Northwest in the early 1790s.
vQ3569: A West African river largely forming the border between Senegal and Mauritania.
Managed jointly since 1972 by Mali, Mauritania and Senegal (later joined by Guinea) through a shared river basin organisation.
Dammed at Manantali and Maka-Diama for irrigation and hydropower.
r1159104001: A large peninsula in Russia's extreme northwest, mostly within the Arctic Circle, bordered by the Barents and White Seas.
Became heavily industrialised and militarized in the Soviet era due to its strategic ice-free Atlantic coast and apatite deposits.
Historically home to the Sámi people before Russian settlement expanded from the 12th century on.
l1159113251: Europe's second-largest lake after Lake Ladoga, located in northwestern Russia.
Home to Kizhi Island's wooden church complex, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and ancient rock petroglyphs on its eastern shores.
r1159103419: The largest and most populous island of Trinidad and Tobago, lying just off Venezuela's coast on the South American continental shelf.
The southernmost island in the Caribbean.
r1159103855: An uninhabited Russian Arctic archipelago of 192 islands, about 85% covered by glaciers.
First reliably documented by the 1873 Austro-Hungarian North Pole expedition, which named it after Emperor Franz Joseph I.
Became part of the Russian Arctic National Park in 2012 after being a protected nature sanctuary since 1994.
r1159102763: An Indonesian island in the Lesser Sundas, separated from Bali by the Lombok Strait.
Shares cultural ties with neighboring Bali despite being administratively distinct, within West Nusa Tenggara province.
r1159103471: The third-largest and most populated of the Hawaiian Islands, home to the state capital Honolulu.
Site of Pearl Harbor and well-known landmarks such as Waikīkī and Diamond Head.
vQ118771: The largest left tributary of the Amazon and the world's largest blackwater river, rising in Colombia and flowing into Brazil.
Despite its huge flow, it carries an unusually low sediment load, giving it its dark, tea-colored water.
r1159102343: The easternmost of Spain's Canary Islands, about 125 km off the African coast.
Known for the volcanic Timanfaya National Park and designated a UNESCO biosphere reserve in 1993.
Named after Genoese navigator Lancelotto Malocello, who first charted it.
r1159104281: The largest island in Papua New Guinea's Bismarck Archipelago, formed largely by volcanic activity.
A major 1994 eruption of the volcano Tavurvur buried the provincial capital Rabaul in ash, forcing the capital to move to nearby Kokopo.
Known during German colonial rule as Neupommern ('New Pomerania').
vQ118251: The Amazon's biggest tributary by volume, flowing through Brazil and Bolivia and supplying about 15% of the Amazon basin's water.
m1159119103: A gulf at the northern end of the Red Sea, west of the Sinai Peninsula, marking part of the boundary between Africa and Asia.
Leads to the Egyptian city of Suez and the entrance of the Suez Canal, making it a key maritime corridor.
r1159104439: The northernmost part of mainland Antarctica, protruding roughly 1,300 km toward South America across the Drake Passage.
Subject to overlapping, internationally unrecognised sovereignty claims by Argentina, Chile and the United Kingdom.
One of the most rapidly warming regions on Earth, with declining sea ice and shifting penguin populations.
l1159113235: Sweden's largest lake and the largest in the European Union, draining to the Kattegat via the Göta älv.
Linked to Lake Vättern and the east coast by the 19th-century Göta Canal.
m1159115503: An arm of the Pacific along Alaska's southern coast, lined with glaciers including the Malaspina and Bering glaciers.
Home to Lituya Bay, site of the largest tsunami ever recorded.
Kept ice-free year-round by the warm North Pacific Current.
r1159103881: The eastern portion of southern Africa's Great Escarpment, forming much of the border between South Africa and Lesotho.
Stretches more than 1,000 km and includes features like the Blyde River Canyon and Three Rondavels in Mpumalanga.
l1159106791: The largest freshwater lake in Central America, of tectonic origin, located in Nicaragua.
Was long considered as a route for an interoceanic canal before the Panama Canal was built instead.
Historically raided by Caribbean pirates who attacked the lakeside city of Granada.
m1159117373: A strait separating Tasmania from mainland Australia, formed about 8,000 years ago by rising sea levels.
Named after English explorer George Bass, who helped prove Tasmania was an island.
p1159104847: A flat, sparsely populated island in Antigua and Barbuda, dominated by the Codrington Lagoon.
Nearly destroyed by Hurricane Irma in 2017, which forced the evacuation of the entire population to Antigua.
l1159113295: Finland's largest lake and the fourth-largest natural freshwater lake in Europe, located in the Finnish Lakeland.
r1730071319: A Polynesian archipelago in French Polynesia, home to Tahiti, its largest and most populous island.
Other major islands in the group include Bora Bora, Moʻorea and Raʻiātea.
vQ171009: A tributary of the Danube flowing from Italy's South Tyrol through Austria and Slovenia into Croatia.
Forms much of the border between Croatia and Hungary before joining the Danube near Osijek.
m1159120609: A strait separating Zealand (Denmark) from Scania (Sweden), one of four waterways linking the Baltic to the Atlantic.
Crossed by the Øresund Bridge since 2000, connecting Copenhagen and Malmö in a shared metropolitan region of nearly 4 million.
Formed about 8,500 years ago when rising seas opened the modern salt-water Baltic Sea.
r1159104237: A fertile valley in Central Asia split between Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan, watered by the Naryn and Kara Darya rivers.
Founded as Alexandria Eschate by Alexander the Great over 2,300 years ago, later home to Mughal founder Babur.
Ethnically mixed and often tense due to border lines drawn during the Soviet era that cut across local communities.
e1159106177: The highest mountain in Canada and the second-highest in North America after Denali, in Yukon's Kluane National Park.
Believed to have the largest base circumference of any non-volcanic mountain on Earth.
Still slowly rising due to ongoing tectonic uplift.
vQ201463: An extensive river system in southern China that flows through Guangzhou and empties into the South China Sea.
China's third-longest river system after the Yangtze and Yellow rivers, and second-largest by volume.
Its wide estuary, the Pearl River Delta, separates Hong Kong and Shenzhen from Macau and Zhuhai.
r1159102385: The northwesternmost of Spain's Canary Islands, home to the Caldera de Taburiente National Park.
Gave the word 'caldera' to geology, after 19th-century geologist Leopold von Buch studied its volcanic crater.
Its Roque de los Muchachos is the second-highest peak in the Canaries after Tenerife's Teide.
r1159103823: A group of islands off northeastern New Guinea, part of Papua New Guinea's Islands Region.
vQ181482: Australia's third-longest river, meeting the Murray River at Wentworth after flowing from northern New South Wales.
Suffers from over-allocation to irrigation, pollution and drought, with the river barely flowing during the 2019 crisis.
m1159118365: A bay of the Baltic Sea between Latvia and Estonia, partly sheltered by Estonia's Saaremaa island.
Connects to the open Baltic mainly through the narrow Irbe Strait.
vQ186541: A left-bank tributary of the Congo River, rising in Angola and forming part of the Angola-DRC border.
Known for its diamond deposits; around 60% of Belgium's diamonds are sourced via the Kasai.
r1159103327: The Mediterranean coastal strip of southeast France, also called the Côte d'Azur, stretching from the Esterel massif to the Italian border at Menton.
Became a winter resort for the British upper class in the late 18th century, later drawing artists like Picasso and Matisse.
The microstate of Monaco sits as an enclave within the region.
r1159104287: The four largest Indonesian islands - Borneo, Java, Sulawesi and Sumatra - grouped together in the Sunda Islands.
Known for exceptional ecological diversity and rich, varied local cultures.
vQ156054: A major Brazilian river flowing about 2,450 km south to north, giving its name to the state of Tocantins.
Though near the Amazon basin, it empties into the Atlantic through its own channel rather than the Amazon River itself.
r1159103425: A rugged island forming part of Nova Scotia, linked to the mainland by the Canso Causeway.
Dominated at its centre by the saltwater inlet Bras d'Or ('Golden Arm').
r1159102573: A remote New Zealand-administered archipelago about 800 km east of the South Island, including the country's easternmost point.
First settled by the Moriori people, who were nearly exterminated after an 1835 Māori invasion.
Keeps its own time zone, 45 minutes ahead of mainland New Zealand.
m1159116143: A warm sea bordering India, the Maldives and Sri Lanka, rich in marine biodiversity.
Named after the Laccadive (Lakshadweep) Islands in its northwest.
m1159117105: A small Mediterranean sea between Spain's mainland and the Balearic Islands, fed by the Ebro River.
r1159102851: Equatorial Guinea's main island, home to the former capital Malabo, located off the coast of Cameroon.
Africa's fourth-largest island, part of the volcanic Cameroon line, with Pico Basile as its highest peak.
r1159102571: A remote Chilean archipelago in the South Pacific, made up of Robinson Crusoe, Alejandro Selkirk and Santa Clara islands.
Named after its 1570s discoverer; sailor Alexander Selkirk was marooned here for over four years, inspiring Daniel Defoe's Robinson Crusoe.
e1159107313: An active stratovolcano in the Philippines whose 1991 eruption was the second-largest terrestrial eruption of the 20th century.
Cooled global temperatures by about 0.5°C for several years by injecting huge amounts of ash and sulfur dioxide into the stratosphere.
Timely evacuation ahead of the eruption, which coincided with a typhoon, saved tens of thousands of lives.
r1159104247: The 'Empty Quarter', a vast desert covering most of the southern Arabian Peninsula across Saudi Arabia, Oman, the UAE and Yemen.
Part of the larger Arabian Desert, one of the driest and most remote regions on Earth.
p1159104715: The largest island of the Chagos Archipelago in the central Indian Ocean, used as a joint UK-US military base since the 1970s.
Its original Chagossian population was forcibly removed between 1968 and 1973 to make way for the base.
Under a 2025 treaty, sovereignty is set to transfer from the UK to Mauritius while the base stays under British control for decades.
e1159105889: An isolated four-peaked volcano massif in Armenia, whose northern summit is the highest point in the country and the Lesser Caucasus.
Covers about a fifth of Armenia's total land area.
m1159116881: A strait between Borneo and Sulawesi in Indonesia, linking the Celebes Sea to the Java Sea.
An important regional shipping route, with ports including Makassar and Balikpapan.
r1159104223: A vast fertile plain across northern India, Pakistan, Nepal and Bangladesh, named for the Indus and Ganges rivers that built it.
Formed from alluvium deposited by the Indus, Ganges and Brahmaputra rivers, making it one of the world's most densely populated and farmed regions.
r1159103103: A sub-alpine range just north of the Western Alps, forming much of the French-Swiss border.
Continues as the unfolded 'Table Jura' through northern Switzerland and Germany.
r1159104279: A scattered Pacific archipelago north of New Guinea, divided between the Federated States of Micronesia and Palau.
Once governed from Manila as part of the Spanish East Indies, earning the historical name 'New Philippines'.
m1159115891: A major inlet between South Wales and South West England, extending from the Severn Estuary to the Atlantic.
Formerly known as the Severn Sea, a name still used in Welsh and Cornish.
r1159104165: A rugged mountainous region across Ethiopia and Eritrea, often called the 'Roof of Africa' for its height and extent.
Bisected by the Great East African Rift System, part of the rift chain stretching from Syria to Mozambique.
m1159116661: An Arctic sea route through Canada's Arctic Archipelago linking the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.
First fully navigated by ship in 1903-1906 by Norwegian explorer Roald Amundsen, after centuries of failed European attempts.
Canada claims it as internal waters while the US and others argue it is an international strait.
r1159103401: A Philippine island in the Visayas, among the country's most populous islands with cities including Tacloban and Ormoc.
Site of significant geothermal power generation near Ormoc.
r1159104067: A region of the northeastern Sahara spanning eastern Libya, Egypt's Western Desert and northwestern Sudan.
Among the most arid, least populated parts of the Sahara, historically blocking trans-Saharan caravan trade due to scarce water.
e1159106093: The highest volcano in North America and Mexico's tallest peak, on the Trans-Mexican Volcanic Belt.
Currently dormant, with its last eruption in the 19th century; the second most topographically prominent volcano on Earth after Kilimanjaro.
r1159102823: Also called Bear Island, the southernmost island of Norway's Svalbard archipelago, discovered by Dutch explorers in 1596.
Uninhabited except for a meteorological station; became a Norwegian nature reserve in 2002.
r1159103653: An Iranian desert of salt flats and dunes in Kerman and Sistan-Baluchestan provinces.
Holds the record for the highest land surface temperature ever measured on Earth, 70.7°C.
Added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2016.
m1159120685: A tidal estuary in California that gives its name to the San Francisco Bay Area, dominated by San Francisco, San Jose and Oakland.
Drains about 40% of California's water via the Sacramento and San Joaquin rivers before meeting the Pacific through the Golden Gate strait.
A Ramsar Wetland of International Importance since 2013, with the Port of Oakland among the busiest on the US west coast.
r1159103599: A range running along Turkey's southern Black Sea coast in northern Anatolia.
Known in Roman times as the Paryadres Mountains.
p1159104707: An uninhabited volcanic island off southern Iceland that emerged from the sea in a 1963-1967 eruption.
Named after Surtr, a fire giant from Norse mythology, and intensively studied as plant and animal life colonised it from scratch.
Shrinking steadily from wave erosion; it is expected to remain above sea level until at least 2100.
m1159116501: A strait in Nunavut linking the Atlantic and Labrador Sea to Hudson Bay, between Baffin Island and Quebec's Nunavik.
Named after English explorer Henry Hudson, who sailed it in 1610 aboard the ship Discovery.
r1159102685: Samoa's second-largest and most populous island, formed by a basaltic shield volcano, home to the capital Apia.
Has no historically recorded eruptions, though evidence shows lava flows within the past few thousand years.
r1159104009: A long peninsula extending from mainland Alaska toward the Aleutian Islands, separating the Pacific Ocean from Bristol Bay.
One of several major Alaskan peninsulas, alongside the Kenai and Seward peninsulas.
p1159104971: A cape on Norway's Magerøya island, the northernmost point in Europe reachable by car via European route E69.
Features a 307 m cliff and plateau popular for viewing the midnight sun over the Barents Sea.
m1159120109: A regional sea in eastern Indonesia between Halmahera and the Pacific, part of the Australasian Mediterranean Sea.
Three deep bays - Weda, Buli and Kao - cut into Halmahera island's coast, giving it four large peninsulas.
r1159103109: Iceland's largest ice cap by volume, covering about 8% of the country in its southeast.
The second-largest ice cap by area in Europe after Novaya Zemlya's Severny Island ice cap.
l1159125095: A huge reservoir straddling Egypt and Sudan, created by the Aswan High Dam and named after President Gamal Abdel Nasser.
Its construction required resettling many Nubian people whose land in northern Sudan was flooded.
Egypt refers to its larger share as Lake Nasser, while Sudan calls its portion Lake Nubia.
r1159102347: The largest island of Seychelles, home to the capital Victoria and about 86% of the country's population.
Named after Bertrand-François Mahé de La Bourdonnais, an 18th-century French colonial governor.
r1159103399: The Philippines' fourth-largest and third most populous island, part of the Visayas group.
Its southern coastal waters lie within the Coral Triangle, a region of exceptionally high marine biodiversity.
r1159104277: A chain of 11 volcanic atolls in the central Pacific, split between Kiribati and US territories, stretching over 2,350 km.
Kiritimati, part of the chain, has the largest land area of any atoll in the world.
The International Date Line runs through the islands, placing Kiribati's portion in UTC+14, the world's most advanced time zone.
l1159106907: The largest alpine lake in North America, straddling the California-Nevada border in the Sierra Nevada.
Known for its exceptionally clear water; its depth of about 501 m makes it the second-deepest lake in the US after Crater Lake.
m1159118407: A Mediterranean gulf on Libya's northern coast, historically known as the Great Sirte or Greater Syrtis.
Named after the oil port of Sidra and the city of Sirte.
r1159102877: The largest island in Alaska's Kodiak Archipelago and the second-largest island in the United States.
Home to the native Kodiak bear and a major US Coast Guard base, with fishing as its leading industry.
e1159105751: The highest peak of the Hindu Kush range and the highest mountain outside the Himalaya-Karakoram system, in Pakistan's Chitral District.
m1159117827: A bay on India's Arabian Sea coast in Gujarat, also known as the Gulf of Cambay, fed by the Narmada, Tapti, Mahi and Sabarmati rivers.
Separates the Kathiawar Peninsula from southeastern Gujarat.
r1159104013: An Argentine peninsula on the Atlantic coast of Chubut Province, bordered by the San Matías Gulf.
A key wildlife reserve, listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1999.
e1159107215: The highest mountain on Java and an active volcano in a subduction zone where the Indo-Australian Plate meets the Eurasian Plate.
Named after Mount Meru (Sumeru), the central mountain of the gods in Hindu cosmology.
vQ26428: A Siberian river that joins the Yenisei at Turukhansk, forming the western edge of the Lena Plateau.
Ice-free only from mid-June to early October due to its far northern location.
r1159103891: A triangular mountain massif in northern Niger's Sahara, rising over 1,800 m and forming an island of Sahel climate amid desert.
Supports pastoral and farming communities and notable prehistoric archaeological sites.
r1159104471: An Antarctic island group in the Drake Passage, about 120 km north of the Antarctic Peninsula.
Claimed without international recognition by the UK, Chile and Argentina, with sovereignty held in abeyance under the Antarctic Treaty.
Home to numerous research stations, mostly on King George Island.
l1159127099: New Zealand's largest lake by surface area, sitting in the caldera of the Taupō supervolcano on the North Island.
Gives its name to the town of Taupō on its northeastern shore.
m1159120253: A sea between the Visayas and Mindanao in the Philippines, also called the Mindanao Sea.
Connects to the Philippine Sea, Camotes Sea and Sulu Sea through several straits.
r1159103917: A discontinuous mountain range running 1,750 km along India's eastern coast, meeting the Western Ghats at the Nilgiris.
Formed in the Archeozoic era as part of the ancient supercontinents Rodinia and Gondwana.
Crossed by major rivers including the Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri as they flow to the Bay of Bengal.
r1159104541: An Antarctic island group in the Southern Ocean, claimed without international recognition by Britain and Argentina.
Hosts Argentina's Orcadas base, established in 1904, and Britain's Signy Research Station, founded in 1947.
e1159108555: A dormant stratovolcano on the Argentina-Chile border in the Puna de Atacama, the second-highest active volcano in the world.
Site of the highest-known archaeological location on Earth; the mummified 'Children of Llullaillaco' were found at its summit in 1999, believed to be human sacrifices.
r1159102841: The largest and most populous island of São Tomé and Príncipe, lying in the Gulf of Guinea just north of the Equator.
Home to about 96% of the country's population.
r1159103921: A mountain range in China's Fujian province known for producing famous oolong and black teas, including Da Hong Pao and lapsang souchong.
A UNESCO World Heritage Site valued for its rare endemic plants and dramatic river valleys.
e1159105691: The highest mountain in Tajikistan and in the former Soviet Union, located in the Pamir Range.
Named after Ismail Samani, a ruler of the medieval Samanid Empire.
l1159126631: A closed-off freshwater lake in the central Netherlands, named after the IJssel river that flows into it.
r1159102361: An island in the Azores whose volcano, Ponta do Pico, is the highest mountain in Portugal.
Known as the 'Black Island' for its volcanic soil, which nourishes UNESCO-listed vineyards.
The youngest and second-largest island in the Azores, formed around 300,000 years ago.
r1159103609: A mountain system stretching over 300 km across northern Spain, from the Pyrenees to the Galician Massif along the Cantabrian Sea.
Popular for hiking and skiing, with resorts including Alto Campoo and San Isidro.
e1159105855: The highest point in Georgia, on the Georgia-Russia border in the Greater Caucasus range.
The third-highest peak in the Caucasus, behind Dykh-Tau and standing southeast of Mount Elbrus, Europe's highest mountain.
r1159102345: A Tanzanian island in the Zanzibar Archipelago, part of the Swahili Coast in the Indian Ocean.
r1159104317: A vast lowland covering parts of Belgium, the Netherlands, Germany, Denmark and Poland, between the Central European Highlands and the North Sea/Baltic coasts.
Connects to the East European Plain, together forming most of the Great European Plain.
p1159104827: The largest and most populous island of the Cook Islands, home to about 72% of the country's population.
Its capital, Avarua, hosts the national parliament and international airport.
Settled by Polynesians late in the first millennium, well before European contact in 1814.
l1159126901: A crater lake in Djibouti, the lowest point on land in Africa at 155 m below sea level.
One of the saltiest bodies of water on Earth, about ten times saltier than the ocean, with salt extracted commercially from its shores.
m1159116431: A bay at the southern end of Hudson Bay, bordered by Quebec and Ontario, with its waters and islands in Nunavut.
Extensively modified by dams for major hydroelectric projects, while remaining the last part of Hudson Bay to freeze and the first to thaw.
r1159103307: A plain occupying most of modern Hungary, the largest part of the wider Pannonian Plain.
Shrank in extent after the 1920 Treaty of Trianon redrew Hungary's borders following World War I.
r1730070601: The world's second-largest coral atoll after Kiritimati, part of the Seychelles' remote Outer Islands.
Lies about 1,120 km southwest of the Seychelles capital, Victoria.
p1159104811: An uninhabited raised coral atoll in the Pitcairn Islands group, part of a British Overseas Territory.
One of only two raised atolls in the world with ecosystems largely untouched by humans, alongside Aldabra; a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1988.
e1159105613: Taiwan's highest mountain, giving the island the fourth-highest high point of any island in the world.
Protected within Yushan National Park, Taiwan's largest and least accessible national park.
Known during Japanese colonial rule as Mount Niitaka.
e1159105935: The highest mountain in Norway, Scandinavia and Northern Europe, located in Jotunheimen National Park.
vQ171847: A major Brazilian river and tributary of the Tocantins River.
r1730072581: A 1,500 km system of mountain ranges and escarpments along Brazil's southeastern coast.
r1159104543: A mountainous South Atlantic island, part of the British Overseas Territory of South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands.
First landed on and claimed for Britain by Captain James Cook in 1775, who named it after King George III.
Served historically as a whaling base, most notably at Grytviken; its research station today has a population of about 20.
m1159117781: Norway's longest and deepest fjord, nicknamed the 'King of the Fjords', stretching 205 km inland in Western Norway.
r1159103289: A desert in northern Saudi Arabia known for violent winds and large crescent-shaped reddish dunes.
Connected to the Rub' al Khali desert by the long gravel-and-dune corridor known as the Dahna.
Site of an 85,000-year-old fossilised human finger found in 2016, among the earliest evidence of modern humans outside Africa.
e1159105621: Japan's most active volcano, a former island now connected to Kyushu as a peninsula.
Its fertile volcanic soil produces the famous Sakurajima daikon radish and komikan orange.
l1159107259: A freshwater lake in Nicaragua, also called Lake Xolotlán, on whose southwestern shore the capital Managua sits.
r1159102407: An uninhabited island in Canada's Arctic Archipelago, part of Nunavut, separated from neighboring islands by several straits and channels.
Canada's twelfth-largest island, home to the seasonal Arctic Watch Lodge.
r1159103013: The highest mountain range on mainland Australia, part of the Great Dividing Range in the southeast.
The only Australian mainland region with annual deep snowfall, comprising the Snowy Mountains and the Victorian Alps.
r1159104219: A vast tropical grassland plain east of the Andes in Colombia and Venezuela.
A major tropical savanna ecoregion supporting extensive cattle ranching.
r1159103497: A 300-mile archipelago of about 1,100 islands off southeastern Alaska, sheltering the northern Inside Passage.
Home to the Tlingit and Kaigani Haida peoples, with Ketchikan and Sitka as its largest towns.
Mostly within the Tongass National Forest, with fishing, logging and tourism as main industries.
l1159113637: A mountain lake on the Tibetan Plateau north of the Nyenchen Tanglha range, also called 'Heavenly Lake'.
vQ270627: A river in central Argentina marking most of the border between Neuquén and Mendoza provinces.
Dammed at Casa de Piedra to generate hydroelectricity and regulate water levels in the arid region it crosses.
m1159117955: A UNESCO World Heritage Site in Western Australia known for its stromatolites, some of the oldest life forms on Earth.
Home to one of the largest and most diverse seagrass beds in the world and a large population of dugongs.
r1730071661: One of the highest mountain ranges on the Arabian Peninsula, shared between Oman and the UAE.
Separates Oman's low coastal plain from the high desert plateau inland.
r1159104025: A large mountainous plateau in Siberian Russia, near the restricted city of Norilsk.
Contains some of the world's largest known nickel deposits.
e1159105943: Romania's highest mountain peak, in the Făgăraș Mountains of the Southern Carpathians.
Had a distant star named after it, XO-1, in 2019.
xQ333946: The longest glacier in the Karakoram and second-longest outside the polar regions, in Indian-administered Ladakh.
Militarized since 1984, it is the site of an ongoing India-Pakistan territorial dispute at extremely high altitude.
Lies in a heavily glaciated region of the Karakoram sometimes called the 'Third Pole'.
m1159118715: A sea along East Antarctica's coast between the West Ice Shelf and Shackleton Ice Shelf.
Discovered by the Australian Antarctic Expedition (1911-1914) and named for Captain John King Davis.
r1159102833: The second-largest island in Norway's Svalbard archipelago, mostly covered by ice caps.
Uninhabited and entirely within the Nordaust-Svalbard Nature Reserve, home to reindeer and walruses.
r1730072595: A 1.7-billion-year-old Precambrian geological formation in northeast South America, home to the tepui table-mountains.
Source of famous waterfalls including Angel Falls and Kaieteur Falls.
r1159104205: A low-lying desert basin stretching from southern Turkmenistan through Uzbekistan into Kazakhstan.
p1159105027: The second-largest of Chile's Juan Fernández Islands, renamed in 1966 to honor its literary connection.
Home to marooned sailor Alexander Selkirk from 1704 to 1709, who partly inspired Daniel Defoe's Robinson Crusoe.
e1159107269: The highest mountain in Sumatra and an active stratovolcano, within Kerinci Seblat National Park.
Home to the endangered Sumatran tiger amid its surrounding rainforest.
l1159115773: A high-altitude endorheic lake split between Indian-administered Ladakh and Chinese-administered Tibet.
The Line of Actual Control passes through it, making it a flashpoint in the Sino-Indian border dispute, including clashes in 1962 and 2020-2021.
vQ213067: A river connecting Lake Onega to Lake Ladoga, Europe's two largest lakes, in Russia's Leningrad Oblast.
Part of the Volga-Baltic Waterway since Peter the Great linked it to the Neva in the 18th century.
r1159103293: A region spanning Tanzania and Kenya famous for hosting one of the world's largest land animal migrations.
Renowned for its large lion population and high biodiversity of large mammals and birds.
r1159104323: The sedimentary basin of the Congo River in Central Africa, containing Africa's largest rainforest.
Second in size only to the Amazon rainforest and an important global carbon sink.
e1159107349: An active stratovolcano on Lombok, Indonesia's second-highest volcano, holding the crater lake Sagara Anak.
Sacred to the indigenous Sasak people, who hold ceremonies at the mountain and its lake.
Its 1257 eruption is considered one of the most powerful volcanic events of the last 2,000 years.
r1159102371: The northwesternmost and second-largest island of Cape Verde, part of the Barlavento Islands group.
r1159103211: A highland region in central Guinea, roughly corresponding to the historic Middle Guinea area of West Africa.
r1730073913: A major mountain range running about 1,100 km through Laos, Vietnam and northeastern Cambodia.
e1159106027: A mountain massif in northwestern Montenegro, part of the Dinaric Alps, bounded by the Tara and Piva river canyons.
Its national park, founded in 1952, became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1980.
e1159107023: Iceland's highest point, a pyramidal peak on the rim of the Öræfajökull volcano's summit crater.
m1159117203: A gulf of the Pacific off southern Panama, where the Panama Canal links to the Pacific side.
Panama City sits on its shore, with the 200-plus-island Pearl Islands archipelago nearby.
r1159103257: A desert in the Afar Triangle spanning Ethiopia, Eritrea and Djibouti, among the hottest and lowest places on Earth.
Known for active volcanoes and extreme heat exceeding 50°C, with local Afar people mining salt there.
r1159103879: The highest section of Morocco's Atlas Mountains, home to Jbel Toubkal, North Africa's highest peak.
Acts as a weather barrier separating the Sahara from Morocco's Mediterranean north.
Home to Berber communities who developed efficient Agdal garden-farming techniques in the dry highlands.
vQ171436: A river in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
m1159116059: A bay in the southern Gulf of Mexico, forming the north side of the Isthmus of Tehuantepec, bordered by three Mexican states.
r1159103543: A mountain range in central Mongolia, about 400 km west of the capital Ulaanbaatar.
l1159106775: A freshwater lake between Ontario and Michigan, linking Lake Huron to Lake Erie via the St. Clair and Detroit rivers.
Not one of the five Great Lakes, but part of the connected Great Lakes system; a maintained shipping channel keeps it navigable despite its shallow depth.
vQ817337: Patagonia's main river by drainage basin, formed by the junction of the Limay and Neuquén rivers in Argentina.
Irrigates orchards producing most of Argentina's pears and apples, including about 48% of the Southern Hemisphere's pear crop.
r1730071679: Also known as the Transylvanian Alps, a group of ranges in southern Romania bounded by the Balkan Mountains in Serbia to the south.
e1159105721: A fault-bounded trough in China's Xinjiang region, home to Lake Ayding, among the lowest depressions on Earth.
One of the hottest and driest places in China during summer.
xQ367943: A major glacier in Argentine Patagonia, one of 48 fed by the Southern Patagonian Ice Field, the world's third-largest reserve of fresh water.
A top tourist attraction, named after explorer Francisco Moreno, who helped settle the Andean border dispute between Argentina and Chile.
r1159103977: The delta of the Niger River on Nigeria's Gulf of Guinea coast, historically known for palm oil trade.
A petroleum-rich region notorious for extensive oil pollution from multinational drilling operations.
l1159113927: The largest lake in China's Xinjiang region, fed mainly by the Kaidu River.
Supports an active fishery, with introduced carp species and European perch dominating catches since the 1970s.
r1159103569: A Chinese mountain range running along the eastern edge of the Loess Plateau through Shanxi, Henan and Hebei provinces.
p1159104701: A headland in Greenland and the country's southernmost point, an important navigational landmark.
xQ491677: The highest waterfall in Yosemite National Park, dropping 739 m in total, a major attraction especially in late spring.
r1159103281: A desert in Australia's Northern Territory and Western Australia, among the last parts of the country explored by Europeans.
Its name derives from the Warlpiri word 'Jarnami', referring to rock holes said never to run dry.
r1159103953: A major Mexican mountain range running along the Gulf of California, part of the American Cordillera backbone of the Americas.
r1159104243: A desert zone in central Kazakhstan, also known as the 'Hungry Steppe'.
r1159103587: A range in central India running parallel to the Vindhya Range, dividing the Indo-Gangetic Plain from the Deccan Plateau.
Source of the Narmada River, which drains its northern slope, and the Tapti River, which drains its southern slope.
xQ38120: One of the world's most powerful single-drop waterfalls, on the Potaro River in Guyana.
About four and a half times the height of Niagara Falls and twice the height of Victoria Falls.
r1730073629: A large arid plateau covering much of northern and central Mexico, flanked by the Sierra Madre Occidental and Oriental.
Home to Mexico's major interior cities including Mexico City, Guadalajara and Puebla.
l1159113343: Chile's second-largest lake, in the Los Lagos Region, shaped by glaciers during the Quaternary ice ages.
Offers views of Volcán Osorno, making nearby Puerto Varas a popular tourist town.
xQ183395: A waterfall in Switzerland's Bernese Oberland, famous as the setting for Sherlock Holmes's fatal confrontation with Moriarty in Arthur Conan Doyle's 'The Final Problem'.
r1159103971: A range of the Peruvian Andes containing Huascarán, Peru's highest mountain, and over 700 individual glaciers.
Protected within Huascarán National Park since 1975; its glaciers have shrunk by about a third since the 1970s.
A key year-round water source for northern Peru and part of the country's hydroelectric power supply.
l1159126789: A lake in east-central Kazakhstan, part of the Dzhungarian Gate pass linking Kazakhstan to northwest China.
Its waters have been reputed to have medicinal properties since Silk Road times.
vQ1161204: A river flowing from Lake Nicaragua to the Caribbean, with its southern bank forming part of the Nicaragua-Costa Rica border.
Once eyed as a canal route in the 19th century; home to freshwater bull sharks.
r1159103681: A peninsula in southern Guangdong province, China, whose largest city is Zhanjiang.
l1159107241: Guatemala's largest lake, draining to the Caribbean via the Rio Dulce.
Guarded historically by the colonial fortress Castillo de San Felipe de Lara against pirate attacks.
Home to manatees, jaguars and howler monkeys, making it a popular birdwatching destination.
l1159126917: A saline lake in Kazakhstan, notable as the site where the Soviet Soyuz 23 spacecraft unexpectedly splashed down through ice in 1976.
m1159117579: The southernmost passable body of water on Earth, in Antarctica, discovered by Captain James Clark Ross in 1841.
Serves as the resupply route for McMurdo Station via ice runways and icebreaker-opened shipping channels.
r1159103717: A vast plateau in north-central China formed from wind-blown dust (loess), bordering the Gobi Desert.
One of the largest and thickest loess deposits in the world, home to around 108 million people despite severe wind erosion.
r1159103035: A mountain range running nearly 1,700 km along western Sumatra, mostly volcanic and densely forested.
Home to the supervolcano Toba, whose caldera-forming eruption about 74,000 years ago was among the largest ever recorded.
Protected within a UNESCO World Heritage Site recognizing Sumatra's exceptional rainforest biodiversity.
r1159103689: A plateau in west-central Africa stretching from Nigeria through Cameroon to the Central African Republic.
Source of the Benue River and known for bauxite deposits; named after Fulani leader Modibo Adama.
xQ38580: The tallest man-made waterfall in the world, created by the Romans in 271 BC near Terni, Italy.
r1159102607: A mountain range in Utah forming the western edge of the Rocky Mountains and eastern edge of the Great Basin.
Its name comes from the Ute language, meaning roughly 'mountain pass' or 'low pass over high range'.
r1159103895: A mountain range spanning China's Heilongjiang province and neighboring Russian regions.
xQ805806: A glacier in Pakistan's Karakoram range, surrounded by some of the world's highest peaks including K2.
Rather than retreating like many glaciers, research shows it experiences surges and shifts into neighboring ice flows.
r1159102645: A plateau near the center of Nigeria, giving its name to Plateau State and its capital, Jos.
Developed as a tin-mining hub by the British in the early 20th century, drawing migrant workers from across Nigeria.
r1159103735: A historic narrow corridor in western Gansu, China, linking the country to Central Asia as part of the Northern Silk Road.
A string of oases flanked by the Qilian Mountains and the Mongolian and Tibetan plateaus.
r1159104525: A vast high plateau in East Antarctica, home to the geographic South Pole and the Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station.
Averages about 3,000 m in elevation across roughly 1,000 km.
r1159102987: The largest mountain plateau of its kind in Europe, in central southern Norway.
Home to the Hardangerjøkulen glacier and largely protected within Hardangervidda National Park.
r1159103945: A mountain range in southern Mexico running 1,000 km from Michoacán to the Isthmus of Tehuantepec in Oaxaca.
r1159104633: A peninsula on New Zealand's North Island, sheltering the Hauraki Gulf from the Pacific Ocean.

r1730070755: The largest peninsula in Costa Rica, on the Pacific coast, known for its beaches and tourism.
Home to Nicoya, one of the oldest settlements in Costa Rica.
r1159102635: A dry lakebed remnant of Pleistocene Lake Lahontan in Nevada's Great Basin, part of a national conservation area.

xQ798283: The tallest waterfall in both Tanzania and Zambia, on the border of the two countries near Lake Tanganyika.

xQ7799533: A vast, fast-flowing Antarctic glacier nicknamed the 'Doomsday Glacier' for its potential to raise global sea levels.

xQ1031467: The world's second-largest contiguous extrapolar ice field, straddling the Andes between Chile and Argentina.
A remnant of the Patagonian Ice Sheet that once covered all of southern Chile during the last glacial period.
xQ686835: A waterfall near Lauterbrunnen in Switzerland's Bernese Highlands, dropping 297 m from a hanging valley.

xQ770424: A major outlet glacier in West Greenland near Ilulissat, draining 6.5% of the Greenland ice sheet.

xQ19558: A massive rapid on the Congo River near Matadi, Democratic Republic of the Congo, with one of the highest water discharges of any waterfall on Earth.

xQ1514989: Antarctica's fastest-melting glacier, responsible for about 13% of the continent's ice loss.

xQ617835: The largest piedmont glacier in the world, in southeastern Alaska, roughly the size of Rhode Island.
